title: Automated MCQA Benchmarking at Scale: Evaluating Reasoning Traces as Retrieval Sources for Domain Adaptation of Small Language Models
problem: Scientific knowledge grows rapidly, but evaluation benchmarks lag behind. Traditional benchmarks become stale. Small language models lack domain-specific knowledge without fine-tuning or retrieval augmentation.
motivation: Enable continuous creation of up-to-date evaluation benchmarks from scientific literature and improve small model performance on domain-specific tasks through retrieval-augmented generation.
method: Scalable pipeline automating MCQA generation from scientific paper corpora: PDF parsing, semantic chunking, question generation, model evaluation. Case study: 16,000+ MCQs from 22,000 papers in radiation and cancer biology. Evaluation of small LMs (1.1B-14B) with RAG using paper chunks vs. reasoning traces from GPT-4.
key_novelty: First at-scale automated MCQA benchmark generation with reasoning trace-based retrieval, demonstrating improved small model performance on domain-specific expert exams.
contributions: PDF parsing and semantic chunking automation
Small models (1.1B-14B) surpassing GPT-4 on 2023 Astro Radiation exam
Evaluation on both synthetic and expert-annotated benchmarks
limitations: Limited to single domain (radiation/cancer biology); reasoning trace approach specific to GPT-4; generalizability to other domains and models unclear; expert annotation limited to one exam.
